steps.description:
Do you think a single button could control a car well enough to take you anywhere you want?

Let's try coding a One-Button Toy Car as follows:
  1. The car will keep moving forward when no button is pressed.
  2. Whenever Button D18 is pressed and held down, it will keep spinning.

  3. You can choose the speed, but going slower often gives you better control.
  4. The program will run forever to check for button press.
Recall the If and Repeat While/Until logic blocks.

A robot's movement can be automated or manually controlled. We will be using buttons as our input sensors to incorporate manual control. Sounds simple? You will soon discover designing control takes more that just linking input control to the output.

A Motor block can make the motor turn forever as shown.

The next block will be run immediately once it turns the motor on.


Have you wondered why cars use steering wheels and pedals instead of simply buttons for control? Let's experience controlling the robot with buttons.


Create a program that uses 2 buttons to steer the robot. 

  • One to turn left and another to turn right.
  • When no button is pressed, it will keep moving forward.
  • You can decide the speeds and durations.
  • The robot will keep moving when the program is started.
Put 2 obstacles in the virtual robot space and navigate your robot as shown.


Do you think this simple setup is suitable for controlling a real car?

1. You may use Repeat While/until or If blocks.

2. Movement duration and speed can affect ease of control.

Knowing that it is not easy to control a robot with simple button setup, you decided to add a safety feature to prevent the robot from crashing into obstacles.

Amend your previous code to have the following features:

  • Press one button to steer left and another to steer right.
  • When no button is pressed, move forward. 

  • Press both buttons will reverse the robot.
  • If an obstacle is less than 5cm away, the robot will stop and can only reverse upon both button pressed.
  • You can decide the speeds and durations.
  • The program will keep running.

Put some obstacles around your robot and test it out.


Prioritise your features to see which should be checked first.
